{{2024–25 Big Ten Conference men's basketball standings}}
The '''2024–25 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Maryland, College Park]] during the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. They were led by third-year head coach [[Kevin Willard]] and played their home games at [[Xfinity Center (College Park, Maryland)|Xfinity Center]] in [[College Park, Maryland]], as a member of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. They finished the season 27–9, 14–6 in Big Ten play to finish in a tie for second place. As the No. 2 seed in the [[2025 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they beat [[2024–25 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]] in the quarterfinals before losing to [[2024–25 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] in the semifinals. They received an at-large bid to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 4 seed in the West region. They defeated [[2024–25 Grand Canyon Antelopes men's basketball team|Grand Canyon]] and [[2024–25 Colorado State Rams men's basketball team|Colorado State]] to advance to the Sweet Sixteen. There, they lost to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|eventual champion]] [[2024–25 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]], 87–71.

Following the season, head coach Kevin Willard left the team to take the head coaching position at [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-30 |title=Kevin Willard leaves Maryland for Villanova in messy departure following Terrapins' Sweet 16 run |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/kevin-willard-leaves-maryland-for-villanova-in-messy-departure-following-terrapins-sweet-16-run/ |access-date=2025-04-01 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> On April 1, the school named [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]] head coach [[Buzz Williams]] the team's new head coach.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-01 |title=Maryland hires Buzz Williams: Terps poach Texas A&M coach to replace Kevin Willard after controversial exit |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/maryland-hires-buzz-williams-terps-poach-texas-a-m-coach-to-replace-kevin-willard-after-controversial-exit/ |access-date=2025-04-01 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Previous season==
The [[2023–24 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Terrapins]] finished the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]] 16–17, 7–13 in [[2023–24 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a tie for eleventh place. As the No. 12 seed in the [[2024 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they beat [[2023–24 Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball team|Rutgers]] in the first round,<ref>{{cite web |title=Scott scores 16, Maryland defeats Rutgers 65-51 to advance at Big Ten Tournament |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401625678 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=May 8, 2024 |date=March 13, 2024}}</ref> before losing to [[2023–24 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] in the quarterfinals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Crowl, Blackwell make 7 of Wisconsin's season-high 16 3s in 87-56 win over Maryland in Big Ten |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401625681 |website=ESPN.com |publisher=Associated Press |access-date=June 8, 2024 |date=March 14, 2024}}</ref> The Terrapins received a bid for the [[2024 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]], but declined.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Wolcott |first1=Nicky |title=Maryland men's basketball declined an NIT bid |url=https://dbknews.com/2024/03/19/maryland-mens-basketball-declined-nit-national-invitation-tournament/ |access-date=June 8, 2024 |work=[[The Diamondback]] |date=March 19, 2024}}</ref>
